{"title": "Nothing Gets Out Unescaped: A Run Through MarkupSafe", "premise": "A web page wants to show a comment somebody posted: ``. Printed as-is into HTML, that string stops being text and starts being code \\u2014 it is a cross-site scripting payload. MarkupSafe exists to make the difference between \"text\" and \"markup\" a property of the value itself, carried in its type, so that a template can mix trusted and untrusted pieces and the untrusted ones can only ever arrive as inert characters. This story follows that one untrusted comment from the moment it is handed to `escape()` until it comes back out of a rendered fragment as plain text again, and notes at each step exactly what is guaranteed, what is merely trusted, and who is responsible for which.", "chapters": [{"n": 1, "title": "The Trust Boundary: escape()", "trace_lines": [2, 5], "data_in": "s = '' \\u2014 a plain str of unknown provenance", "data_out": "Markup('<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>')", "code": ["src/markupsafe/__init__.py:24-45", "src/markupsafe/_native.py", "src/markupsafe/_speedups.c:74-171"], "inputs": ["''"], "characters": ["escape", "_escape_inner", "_native._escape_inner", "Markup"], "facts": ["`escape` tests `type(s) is str`, not `isinstance`, so the fast path is taken only by exact `str`; the comment qualifies and skips the `__html__` check entirely (__init__.py:39-40).", "The comment on lines 37-38 says `type(s)` is deliberate: a proxy object can lie about `__class__`, so `isinstance` would be a trust hole; `tests/test_escape.py::test_proxy` pins this.", "`_escape_inner` replaces exactly five characters \\u2014 `&`, `>`, `<`, `'`, `\"` \\u2014 and nothing else (_native.py:1-8).
